Article.ArticleTitle: Effects of humidity, CO<sub>2</sub> and O<sub>2</sub> on real time quantitation of breath biomarkers by means of PTR-ToF-MS.

Abstract.AbstractText: Proton-transfer-reaction-time-of-flight-mass-spectrometry (PTR-ToF-MS) represents an attractive tool for real-time analysis of VOC profiles in human breath. Quantification of breath VOCs by means of direct MS may be affected by the matrix as human breath does not only contains several hundred VOCs in the ppbV-pptV level but is water saturated and contains percentage levels of CO2. Investigation of breath biomarkers in clinical studies requires quantitative and comparable results. We, therefore, assesed systematically the effect of humidity, CO2 and O2 onto the results of PTR-MS analysis. We investigated more than 20 VOCs including aldehydes, ketones, aromatic compounds and hydrocarbons with different sample humidities, CO2 and O2 content. The influence of data processing (e.g. normalization onto H3O+ ion count) was also addressed.  An increase of the H3O+ count of about 20 % was observed when humidity in the sample was increased to breath levels. Large differences regarding measured VOC intensities were found between dry and humid samples. Data normalization on H3O+ or water clusters could not fully compensate the humidity dependent effects. However, as determination of most VOCs linearly depended on humidity over the whole investigated range, a factor based correction seems possible. Effects of CO2 were more pronounced in dry samples than in humid samples but had only minor influence on results. The same was true for the influence of O2.  For reliable quantification of VOCs in clinical studies and for standardization of VOC research well-adapted calibration standards are required for PTR-MS analysis.&#13.
